checks: Verified the exact source locator 9040ddab36f28107 §2, (5)–(8), including the surviving pure parameter term and the precise strict second-order scope.

The first-stress predecessor applies on the same W,theta product chart. The two derivatives of total mass minus ell-weighted cap mass vanish because ell·f(B)=V tr B and ell·DG(0)=0. A critical cap velocity therefore has zero mass derivative.

In the full Hessian of F_i(W,theta)-F_i(I,theta)+G_i(theta), the two pure theta terms involving F cancel at W=I, while the W and W-theta terms remain. This leaves D^2G_i, on the actual original source. The coefficient of the mixed derivative is two.

A physical acceleration R(-q-gamma Q 1/2) adds exactly -q-gamma Q 1/2 to the cap accelerations. Its Lagrangian effect is zero by stationarity. Since sum ell_i=1/gamma, the mass second derivative is Q/2. Taylor expansion on the C^2 chart gives the strict finite changes for small positive time.

For the converse the acceleration term drops out of the Lagrangian second derivative at a stationary point. Positive mass acceleration and strictly negative cap accelerations then give positive Q because all ell_i>0.
